# Buyer Quirk Sheet — Air Traffic and Navigation Services Company Limited (ATNS)

**Buyer:** Air Traffic and Navigation Services SOC Ltd (ATNS), Republic of South Africa
**Kind:** National State-Owned Company (SOC) — commercialised air navigation service provider (ANSP), established under the ATNS Company Act (Act 45 of 1993)
**Packs sampled:** 8 — ocds-9t57fa-165871, ocds-9t57fa-165586, ocds-9t57fa-165430, ocds-9t57fa-165747, ocds-9t57fa-164776, ocds-9t57fa-164792, ocds-9t57fa-164968, ocds-9t57fa-165881
**Date compiled:** 2026-08

Pack index (for citation context):
- **165871** — RFQ04/04/2026/27, "GRC Compliance Professional" (appointment of a Compliance, Risk & Governance service provider)
- **165586** — RFP12/06/2026/27, "BS_FLEET_MANAGEMENT" (Fleet Management services, national)
- **165430** — RFQ12/05/2026/27, "ATA_Fans_Hardrives/Re-advert" (supply and delivery, ATA)
- **165747** — RFP/23/07/2026, "FABL_FAUP_FAKM_CLEANING AND HYGIENE SERVICES" (Bloemfontein region)
- **164776** — RFQ, service provider appointment, City of Ekurhuleni locality
- **164792** — RFQ, catering/labour-type service provider (Free State region references)
- **164968** — RFQ/03/2026/52, "FACT_Supply of Labour Re-advert" (skilled/unskilled labour, Cape Town Station)
- **165881** — RFQ0050/MARK/TS/2024/2025/Adobe Creative (3 Adobe Creative Cloud licences, low-value RFQ)

---

## 1. Submission channel & rules

ATNS runs **three distinct submission regimes depending on procurement size/complexity**, and is explicit that mixed-channel submissions are not freely interchangeable:

- **Large/complex RFPs — dual channel (online OR hard copy), no observed precedence rule.** Fleet Management (165586) and Cleaning & Hygiene (165747) both state: *"Submissions can be made online or via hard copy."* (165586 L1606; 165747 L811). Hard copy has a specific format: *"Hard copy submissions: Include one original, one copy, and one PDF version on USB."* (165586 L1609; 165747 L814) delivered to "ATNS Company Limited, Eastgate Office Park, Block C, South Boulevard Road, Bruma, 2298." No clause in either sampled pack states which copy governs if online and hard-copy versions conflict — **not observed in sampled packs**.
- **Standard RFQs/RFPs — online-only via National Treasury e-Submission (e-Tender), email explicitly barred.** 165430, 165747 (cover page) and 164776/164792/164968 all carry: *"BID SUBMISSION - ONLINE All bid submissions must be made via the e-Submission (e-Tender) system"* with the note *"Submissions sent via email will not be accepted or processed."* (165430 L68-70; near-identical wording repeated in 164776, 164792, 164968, and on the 165586/165747 cover pages).
- **Low-value RFQs — email to a dedicated mailbox, hand delivery barred.** The Adobe Creative Cloud RFQ (165881) instead requires: *"Bidders must email a soft copy of their proposal to: RFQs@atns.co.za and copy lesedima@atns.co.za"* and states on the cover page *"Note: All responses must be submitted on the above dedicated mailbox. No hand delivery submissions will be considered."*
- **Late bids barred** (standard SBD1 Part B boilerplate present across packs): *"Bids must be delivered by the stipulated time to the correct address. late bids will not be accepted for consideration."* (165881; same clause recurs in the GCC/SBD1 sections of other packs).
- Bids must be split into labelled **parcels** submitted together: typically Parcel A (Administrative + Mandatory), Parcel B (Price + Specific Goals), and for technical RFPs a separate Parcel B for Functionality with Price/Specific Goals pushed to Parcel C (165586 L1576-1590: *"Parcel A – Administrative and Mandatory... Parcel B – Functionality / Technical... Parcel C – Price and Specific Goals"*).

## 2. Municipal-arrears / rates clause

**Not observed in sampled packs.** No pack contains a "not more than X days in arrears" municipal rates/utilities clause. The only municipal-document reference found is a **"Municipality Bill"** offered as one of several acceptable *proof-of-address* documents for the "Locality Footprint" mandatory requirement (see §8), not as a good-standing/arrears test — e.g. 164776 L497: *"a. Municipality Bill, b. Lease c. Title Deed d. Official letter with stamp from the local Councillor"*.

## 3. B-BBEE treatment

**Preference points only — not a hard pre-qualification gate.** All 8 packs apply the standard PPPFA 80/20 system (all sampled contract values are ≤R50m; the 90/10 threshold above R50m is quoted only as the standard SBD 6.1 boilerplate, never triggered in a sampled pack — e.g. 165871 L1257-1260).

- Typical specific-goals split is **10 points for "51% Black Owned suppliers" + 10 points for "30% Black Woman Owned Suppliers"** = 20 of 100 total points (165871 L688-715; same split in 165586 L1947-1970 and 165430/164776/164792/164968 boilerplate).
- The smallest-value RFQ sampled (Adobe licences, 165881) collapses this to a **single goal, all 20 points on "51% Black Owned Suppliers"**, with no black-woman-owned split.
- Evidence required to *claim* points: B-BBEE certificate/sworn affidavit (EME/QSE), CSD report, CIPC documents, shareholder certificates, ID copies of shareholders (165871 L696-704). Missing evidence only forfeits the points — *"Bidders who fail to submit the above documents will not qualify for points allocated for specific goals"* (165881) — it does not disqualify the bid outright, confirming preference-only treatment.
- **Quirk:** validity-period carve-out — general bid validity is 60 (or 120) days, but *"the priced proposal will remain valid... except for the Tax and B-BBEE certificates which must still be valid at the time of award"* (165881) — i.e. B-BBEE/Tax documents must stay current through to actual award, not just through the standard validity window.

## 4. Cure/condonation policy

ATNS applies a **strict two-tier fatal/curable split**, worded almost identically across every sampled pack:

- **Administrative defects (Stage 1) are curable within 7 days**, but only for non-substantive gaps: *"The Bidder must submit any supplementary information within seven (7) days to achieve full compliance. The supplementary information must strictly address administrative requirements and not be substantive in nature."* (verbatim or near-verbatim in 165871 L517-520, 165586 L1644-1647, 165430 L507-509, 165747 L854-856, 164776 L489-492, 164968 L429-431). ATNS retains discretion even here — it "may" reject outright instead of allowing the cure.
- **Mandatory-requirement defects (Stage 2) are fatal, not curable**: *"Only bidders who fully comply with all mandatory requirements will advance... Failure to comply with any mandatory requirement will result in automatic disqualification"* (165871 L527-529). Individual mandatory items reinforce this — e.g. reference letters: *"Failure to provide these documents will result in automatic disqualification"* (165871 L544-545); uncertified qualification certificates: *"will not be accepted and will be disregarded (no score will be allocated)"* (165871 L589-591) — i.e. zero-scored with no cure path, not merely penalised.
- Pricing-schedule gaps are treated as fatal too, framed as "non-responsive" rather than curable: missing price, incomplete price, or an omitted cost element (fees vs. reimbursables) "will be deemed to be non-responsive" / "may be considered non-responsive" (165430 L793-800).

## 5. Security/vetting requirements

**Not observed in sampled packs.** Despite ATNS being a safety/security-sensitive aviation SOE, none of the 8 packs contain vetting, security-clearance, polygraph, or integrity-pact language for bidders/personnel.

- **POPIA consent is present in every sampled pack**, but as a full multi-clause contractual obligation embedded directly in the tender/GCC document (not a separate signed consent form): *"The Service Provider shall ensure that its employees, representatives and officers, comply with the provisions of the Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 ('POPIA')..."* with liability, breach-notification and processing-limitation sub-clauses (165871 §11, L1578-1630; equivalent clause numbered 41.8/43.8/35.13 in other packs).
- A **Fraud Hotline / whistleblowing channel** (Deloitte Tip-offs) is printed on the cover/header of most packs: *"Fraud Hotline: 0800 222 335 (Freecall number available 24hrs); Email: ATNS@tip-offs.com"* — a standing integrity-reporting mechanism rather than a bidder integrity pact.
- SBD4 Bidder's Disclosure (state-employee/conflict-of-interest declaration) is standard across packs but is PPPFA-mandated boilerplate, not an ATNS-specific vetting regime.

## 6. Financial demands

- **Professional indemnity insurance required, but generically** — no stated Rand amount in any sampled pack: *"a requirement for the tenderer to have adequate professional indemnity insurance"* (165871 L758-759; identical wording in 165881).
- **Performance security** (GCC clause 7) is required as a bank guarantee/irrevocable letter of credit "or a cashier's or certified cheque," but the amount is deferred to the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC), which is **not populated with figures in any sampled pack** (165871 L1866-1883).
- **Goods insurance** (GCC clause 11) is likewise required "in the manner specified in the SCC" with no amount given in-pack.
- **Not observed in sampled packs:** bank confirmation letters, credit ratings, or audited financial statements as a submission requirement. Financial capacity gating is not evidenced in this sample.
- A **retention clause** for non-satisfactory completion is referenced as a standard contract term (165871 L757) but no percentage/amount is specified in the sampled RFx documents themselves.

## 7. Functionality norms

Functionality treatment **varies sharply by procurement complexity** — there is no single fixed threshold:

- **Simple professional-services/labour RFQs** (165871 GRC Compliance, 164968 Labour, 164776/164792) run only **3 stages** — Administrative → Mandatory (pass/fail) → Price/Specific Goals — with no separately scored functionality phase. CV/qualification/reference-letter criteria function as a pass/fail proxy for functionality instead of a scored stage.
- **Complex technical RFP** (165586 Fleet Management) runs a full **4-stage** process with an explicit scored Functionality stage: *"The minimum qualifying threshold for functionality is 76 points out of 100. Any bidder scoring less than 76 points will not be considered for further evaluation."* (165586 L1853-1854). Criteria are objective/checklist-style (e.g. "All 6 requirements met with evidence = 45.00... 4 requirements met = 25.00...").
- **Distinctive escalation:** the same Fleet Management RFP adds a **Stage 4 live "System Demonstration"**, also scored out of 100 but with a **100-point (i.e. 100%) threshold**, where component failure is fatal regardless of aggregate score: *"Failure to demonstrate the Fleet Management System or Driver Identification & Control System shall result in a score of zero for the Demonstration criterion, as these are [core]..."* (165586 L1901-1909) and *"A functionality area shall only be regarded as successfully demonstrated where the bidder demonstrates all key requirements... using a live system, live process and/or operational evidence."* This is a materially stricter norm than the 76/100 paper-functionality threshold one stage earlier.

## 8. Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **"Locality Footprint" mandatory requirement** — for regionally delivered services, bidders must prove physical presence in the specific municipal/provincial area of performance as a **fatal (Stage 2 mandatory), not preference-scored**, requirement: *"Locality Footprint - Proof of address (City of Ekurhuleni)... a. Municipality Bill, b. Lease c. Title Deed d. Official letter with stamp from the local Councillor or e. Agreement, Memorandum of Understanding with locally based partner"* (164776 L495-503); the same structure recurs for Free State/Northern Cape in 165747 L979-993 (*"Bidder shall submit proof of local presence within the area/station for which they are bidding"*). This is unusual among SOE buyers and ties directly to ATNS's station-based operating model.
- **Live system demonstration with 100%-component pass gate** layered on top of a separately scored paper-functionality stage (see §7) — a two-step functionality gauntlet not seen described elsewhere in the sample.
- **"As-and-when-required" panel/no-minimum-order clause**: *"This bid is based on an 'as-and-when-required' panel arrangement, and ATNS does not guarantee any minimum... Services will be procured on an ad hoc basis, subject to operational requirements and the availability of budget."* (165871 L1160-1162) — bidders are told upfront that winning does not guarantee volume.
- **Document-cure asymmetry**: administrative paperwork gaps get a 7-day fix window, but a single uncertified qualification certificate is discarded outright with zero score and no cure — a meaningfully harsher line than the general "supplementary information" cure clause would suggest at first read.
- **Two/three-parcel structural split** of every bid (Administrative+Mandatory / Functionality / Price+Specific Goals) is applied consistently regardless of RFQ vs RFP format, even down to the small Adobe licence RFQ (which instead uses a 2-stage Administrative → Price/Specific Goals split).
- **Certificate currency to point of award, not just to point of submission** — Tax Compliance and B-BBEE certificates must remain valid "at the time of award," a stricter standard than the general bid-validity period (165881).

---
*Compiled from 8 ATNS tender packs (corpus2). Claims not attributable to a specific pack quote are marked "Not observed in sampled packs" rather than inferred.*
